trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied HTTP/1.1 method string is a valid RFC 9110 token before it is written verbatim into the request line; decided (after the fix) only in Mint.HTTP1.Request.encode/4, the single request-line encoder.

landing_point.why: encode_request_line/2 concatenates method, space, target and ' HTTP/1.1\r\n' with no check; the neighbouring header validators (request.ex:48-68) show the idiom to copy.

fix_sites.module_kind: internal encoder (@moduledoc false) behind public client API

fix_sites.entry_point: new private validate_method!/1 in lib/mint/http1/request.ex, called from encode/4

fix_sites.module_kind: public module, error formatting only (no protection logic)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All HTTP/1 request-line writers funnel through Mint.HTTP1.Request.encode/4 (lib/mint/http1.ex:311, the only caller); UnsafeProxy (lib/mint/unsafe_proxy.ex:86) and TunnelProxy (lib/mint/tunnel_proxy.ex:26, constant "CONNECT") both go through Mint.HTTP1.request/5, so the fix at the choke point covers them.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered method route exists to dismiss; the only arguable neighbour is the documented :skip_target_validation opt-out (lib/mint/http1.ex:130-133, 1045), which concerns the request target, not the method, and is out of this advisory's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Custom/extension token methods (PROPFIND, MKCOL, lowercase or mixed-case methods, symbols like '!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~') must still be sent; a whitelist of standard verbs or an uppercase-only rule would break WebDAV and other extension methods (the fix's own test asserts PROPFIND passes).

O6_input_shapes: method containing other control characters such as TAB

O7_producer.where: Method is passed straight from the caller to the encoder (lib/mint/http1.ex:299-316); no schema, serializer, cache or config loader produces it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Validate the method in Mint.HTTP1.request/5 next to validate_request_target instead of in the encoder, leaving a second encoder caller (e.g. a planted raw-request or pipelining helper) unprotected.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The target check already lives in http1.ex rather than in Request.encode, so a maintainer could plausibly put the method check there too; a WHERE-type sibling only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A configurable CONNECT method or proxy option passed through into HTTP1.request without the encoder check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The proxy path builds request-line components itself from options; a 'custom tunnel method' option would be a natural feature, though still routed through the same encoder.

O9_family: CRLF injection / HTTP request splitting (CWE-93) in the HTTP/1.1 request line

O10_build.toolchain: Elixir + Erlang/OTP, mix (deps fetched once via mix deps.get)
O10_build.project_tests: test/mint/http1/request_test.exs (Request.encode unit tests, offline); test/mint/http1/conn_test.exs uses a local test socket server; integration_test.exs files need network and are tagged separately.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a validate_method!/1 with is_tchar in Request.encode/4, mirroring validate_header_name!/1. This is the published fix, and it is complete.

out_of_scope_notes: The :skip_target_validation option (lib/mint/http1.ex:130-133, 1045) lets a CRLF-bearing target reach the request line unchecked; it is a documented opt-out for the target, not the method.

HTTP/2 sends the method unvalidated as the :method pseudo-header (lib/mint/http2.ex:537-542, 1593-1602); it is HPACK-encoded so there is no CRLF on the wire, but a downgrading intermediary could matter. That is a different sink.
The same release fixes three other advisories (content-length parsing, the HTTP/2 CONTINUATION bound, PUSH_PROMISE limits; fix.diff:17-19). They are not part of this entry.
